name: Masala Omelette
cuisine: Pan-Indian (found in home kitchens, Irani cafés, highway dhabas and Mumbai omelette-pav carts)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ small onion, very finely chopped (about 3 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium tomato, seeds removed, very finely chopped (about 2 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Groundnut oil (or any neutral cooking oil, or ghee)

equipment: 8-inch (20 cm) frying pan or tawa, ideally non-stick
Flat, wide spatula (wooden or silicone is gentlest on non-stick)
Chopping board and a sharp knife
Measuring spoons (normal teaspoons are a fine stand-in)

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Peel and very finely chop 30 g (¼ small) onion.
steps.tip: Chop very fine. The omelette cooks in about 3 minutes, so big pieces stay raw and make it break when you flip.
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even pieces, smaller than a lentil.
steps.cameraCheck: About 3 tbsp chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the onion.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Cut ¼ tomato, scoop out the seeds and watery pulp with a spoon, and very finely chop the flesh (25 g).
steps.tip: Removing the seeds keeps the omelette from turning watery.
steps.visualCue: Small red cubes with no loose seeds or juice.
steps.videoShot: The spoon scooping out the seeds, then the knife dicing.

steps.title: Chop the chilli and coriander
steps.text: Very finely chop ½ green chilli (3 g) and 1 tbsp (3 g) coriander leaves.
steps.tip: Remove the chilli seeds if you want it milder.
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli and coriander side by side

steps.title: Crack the eggs
steps.text: Crack 2 eggs into the bowl, one at a time.
steps.tip: Crack on a flat surface for fewer shell bits. Lift out any shell with a larger piece of shell.
steps.visualCue: Two whole yolks, no shell pieces
steps.videoShot: An egg cracking on the counter edge and opening into the bowl.

steps.title: Add salt and spices
steps.text: Add the salt (a big pinch, 1 g), a pinch of turmeric (0.25 g) and ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder (0.5 g).
steps.visualCue: Small coloured heaps on top of the eggs
steps.cameraCheck: The spices sitting on the eggs
steps.videoShot: The spices sprinkled into the bowl.

steps.title: Beat the eggs
steps.text: Beat with a fork until fully mixed (add the optional 1 tbsp milk now).
steps.tip: Tilt the bowl and whisk briskly; the air you beat in makes the omelette fluffy.
steps.visualCue: An even, golden-yellow mix with a light froth and no streaks of white.
steps.cameraCheck: The beaten eggs in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The fork whisking in quick circles.

steps.title: Mix in the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, tomato, chilli and coriander to the eggs and stir to combine.
steps.visualCue: Vegetables spread evenly through the egg, not sunk in one heap.
steps.cameraCheck: The speckled egg mix in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The fork folding the vegetables in.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Put the pan on medium heat. Add 1½ tsp (7.5 ml) oil and tilt the pan to coat the base.
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmers; a drop of egg sizzles at once. It should not smoke.
steps.cameraCheck: The oiled pan on the flame

steps.title: Pour in the eggs
steps.text: Stir the egg mix once more, then pour it into the pan. Tilt the pan so it spreads into an even circle.
steps.tip: Spread the vegetables with the spatula tip if they bunch in the middle.
steps.visualCue: A gentle sizzle; an even layer about ½ cm thick.
steps.cameraCheck: The egg spread across the pan
steps.videoShot: The speckled egg pouring in and spreading.

steps.title: Let it set
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-low. Leave it untouched.
steps.tip: Cover the pan with a lid for the last 30 seconds if the top stays very wet.
steps.visualCue: The edges turn opaque and lift slightly; the top is mostly set with only a thin wet layer left.
steps.videoShot: Close-up of the edges going from glossy to matte.

steps.title: Loosen the edges
steps.text: Run the spatula around the edge and under the omelette.
steps.visualCue: The omelette slides freely when you shake the pan.
steps.videoShot: The omelette gliding as the pan is shaken.

steps.title: Flip it
steps.text: Slide the wide spatula under the middle and turn the omelette over in one quick move.
steps.tip: If it tears, press it back together; it still tastes the same. Or use the plate trick from the Equipment list.
steps.visualCue: The cooked side is golden with light brown spots.

steps.title: Cook the second side
steps.visualCue: No wet egg at the edges; when pressed lightly in the centre, it feels springy, not liquid.
steps.cameraCheck: The omelette in the pan, second side down
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing the centre gently.

steps.title: Fold and plate
steps.text: Fold the omelette in half (optional) and slide it onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Golden outside, soft and moist inside, with red, white and green flecks.
steps.videoShot: The omelette sliding onto the plate, then a fork cutting into it.

protein.source: Zomato listing, Protein Chef, Marol (Andheri East), "Masala Omelette – High Protein" (egg count and portion weight not stated). The Protein Chef Mulund West and Kharghar listings showed no protein value for this item in snippets.

reasons: two whole eggs give about 13 g of complete protein for about 225 kcal, with only 1½ tsp oil and no frying beyond a quick pan-cook. Onion, tomato, chilli and coriander add flavour and a little fibre. Points come off for the cholesterol and saturated fat in the yolks and for low fibre overall. Café and street versions are often cooked in a tablespoon or more of butter, salted more heavily, and almost always sold with buttered pav or white bread, which can double the calories and add refined flour.

researchRating.basis: the masala omelette is one of India's most common everyday egg dishes, cooked at home, in Irani cafés and at Mumbai omelette-pav carts. Recipe pages rate it highly (The Love of Spice 5/5 from 16 votes; Whisk Affair 4.86/5 from 7 votes; Tiffin and Tea 5/5 from 6 votes; Tarla Dalal 5/5 from 4 reviews with about 132,000 views), and Mumbai food guides list it among the city's favourite egg dishes. Small deductions because vote counts are small and it is seen as a basic, everyday dish rather than a standout one; some café reviews call it ordinary.

storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers can go in the fridge in an airtight box within 2 hours of cooking and keep for up to 2 days (cooked egg dishes are generally safe for 3–4 days, but the omelette turns rubbery after day 1). Freezing is not recommended; it turns watery and spongy when thawed. To reheat, warm in a pan on low heat with a lid for 1–2 min per side, or microwave covered in 15-second bursts until hot all through.
leftoverRemix: Omelette egg-fried rice ("omelette pulao"). Slice the cold omelette into thin strips. Heat ½ tsp oil, add 1 cup cooked rice, a pinch of salt, ¼ tsp pepper and ½ tsp soy sauce, and toss for 2 min. Fold in the omelette strips and a handful of spring onion greens, and toss for 30 sec more.
burnOff: about 3.2 km of running (225 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 4.5 km of brisk walking (about 55 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 buttered pav (about 465 kcal): about 6.6 km running or 9.3 km walking (est.).
